rf.exclusions_hint: A line containing one of these terms (comma-separated) is ignored, even if a keyword matches.
rf.grouping_window_hint: Lines detected during this window are analysed together, in a single AI call.
rf.app_context_hint: Tells the AI what this rule monitors and what is normal here.
rf.context_lines_hint: Read from the source around the detected lines, so the AI sees what happened just before and just after.
rf.notify_closed_hint: with its duration and why it was closed
rf.notify_silent: Alert when the source goes silent
rf.notify_silent_hint: no line received for the chosen duration
rf.resolution_hint: Automatically close an incident when the problem has stopped.
rf.calm_adaptive_hint: Three times the observed interval between the incident's errors, with a minimum. An error that comes back every 2 h waits more than 6 h before being closed.
rf.calm_fixed_hint: Always the same error-free duration, whatever the incident's rhythm.
rf.probe_hint: As long as the probe fails, the incident stays open, even if the log is silent.
rf.success_check: Check when a success line appears
rf.success_check_hint: Patterns are managed in the Resolution tab.
rf.learn: Suggest patterns learned by the AI
rf.learn_hint: added only after you approve them
rf.ai_ambiguous_hint: The AI only checks success lines. A full calm (with a passing probe if configured) closes the incident without an AI call.
rf.ai_always_hint: The AI confirms every closure, including after a full calm. Slower and more expensive.
rf.ai_never_hint: No AI call: the first success line or a full calm closes the incident.
rf.keywords_hint_auto: Comma-separated. You can leave it empty: the AI suggests them from the log.
rf.learn_history: Analyze the last 7 days of the log when the rule is created
rf.tuning_auto_hint: The AI adds missing keywords and removes noise, after checks against your data. Every change can be undone in the Keywords tab.
rf.tuning_suggest_hint: The AI suggests; you approve each change in the Keywords tab.
rf.tuning_off_hint: Keywords only change when you edit them.
rf.ap_badge_title: Set by the autopilot. Change it to take it over.
rf.ap_hint_new_on: Just pick the log to watch. The AI reads its history (or watches it for 24 h if there is none), then manages everything: name, context, keywords, grouping window, silence delay, notification threshold and return-to-normal lines. Everything stays editable afterwards in Settings.
rf.ap_hint_new_off: You set the keywords and the rule settings yourself.
rf.ap_hint_on: The AI manages the whole rule without asking you anything: keywords, context re-read every week, grouping window, silence delay, notification threshold and return-to-normal lines. To see or change what it set, switch to Manual.
rf.ap_hint_off: You manage this rule's settings yourself. The autopilot can take them over anytime.
rf.ap_name_placeholder: Leave empty: the AI will choose it
rf.ap_context_placeholder: Leave empty: the AI will write it from the log
rf.ap_status_observing: Watching until {when}: not enough history. Meanwhile, the rule alerts on error-level lines.
rf.ap_status_cancelled: Setup cancelled. The rule alerts on error-level lines; run a history analysis in the Keywords tab to resume.
rf.ap_status_error: Setup failed ({error}). It will retry automatically in a few hours; meanwhile, the rule alerts on error-level lines.
rf.ap_status_active: Rule set up. The log is re-read every week.
rf.kw_in_tab: Keywords and ignored lines are managed in the Keywords tab, with their statistics and change history.
rf.syslog_none: No line received yet. Set up sending from your source: it will show up here with its first message.
rf.ap_tagline: The AI takes care of everything
rf.ap_hint_enable: When you save, the autopilot re-reads the log history and takes over the grouping window, the silence delay, the notification threshold, the return-to-normal lines, and the context if it is empty. The name and what you wrote are kept.
rf.ap_hint_disable: Settings marked AI were set by the autopilot. Saving in Manual stops it: everything stays as it is and you manage it yourself. You can switch it back on anytime.

diag.title: Diagnostics (read-only)
diag.intro: Lets the AI of the chat and investigations check the actual state of your infrastructure itself (containers, disk, memory, services) instead of asking you to run docker ps or df. Everything is read-only: nothing can be started, stopped or changed.
diag.docker_hint: Through a Docker socket proxy that only allows reads (state, health, restarts, logs, usage). Sentinel never mounts the socket itself.
diag.docker_compose_hint: Add this service to the same docker-compose.yml as Sentinel, then run docker compose up -d. The address http://docker-proxy:2375 is already filled in.
diag.unraid_step1: In the Unraid terminal, create a dedicated network (once): docker network create sentinel. To see it in the network list, enable Settings › Docker › Preserve user defined networks.
diag.unraid_step2: In the Apps tab, install the Log-to-LLM-Sentinel-Docker-Proxy template and pick the sentinel network.
diag.unraid_step3: Edit the Log-to-LLM-Sentinel container and pick the sentinel network too.
diag.unraid_step4: The address http://sentinel-docker-proxy:2375 is filled in: click Test and save.
diag.unraid_no_port: Do not publish the proxy port on your network: even read-only, it exposes the configuration of all your containers.
diag.host_hint: An SSH key generated by Sentinel, allowed on the server only for a script of read-only checks (disk, memory, load, network shares, services). Even if stolen, it allows nothing else.
diag.regenerate_confirm: The old key will stop working: you will need to paste the block on the server again. Continue?
diag.step_install: Paste this block in a terminal on the server.
diag.step_settings: Check the server address and the user shown at the end of the block, then click Test and save.
diag.script_outdated: ⚠ Connected, but the script installed on the server is outdated: paste the step 2 block again to get the latest checks.
diag.need_host: Enter the server address and the user.
diag.install_review: To review it: the header sums up what it does, only the numbered steps change the server, and everything after them is the read-only checks script, commented check by check.
diag.remove_hint: Paste this block in a terminal on the server (platform chosen in step 2): it removes Sentinel's key and the script, so Sentinel can no longer connect. Then forget the server in Sentinel.
diag.forget_confirm: Clear the address and user? The AI will no longer have access to the server.
